17		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/brainstore"
18		bmanifest "github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/manifest"
19	)

21	const (
22		DirName          = "facts"
23		TaxonomyFileName = "taxonomy.json"
24		TaxonomyPath     = DirName + "/" + TaxonomyFileName
25		FileName         = "facts.ndjson"
26		MaxPerChunk      = 6 // quality-gate output cap per source chunk
27	
28		OriginDistilled = "distilled"
29		OriginAuthored  = "authored"
30		OriginImported  = "imported"
31	)

33	// factmerge.Record (factmerge.Record) and factmerge.Anchor (factmerge.Anchor) are defined
34	// as type aliases in facts_aliases.go; the durable-fact data model now lives in
35	// factmerge.
36	
37	// Taxonomy is the active taxonomy snapshot. Paths are validated against
38	// factPathPattern; classification may only invent a new three-level path under
39	// an existing top-level category.
40	type Taxonomy struct {
41		GeneratedAt time.Time         `json:"generated_at"`
42		Categories  map[string]string `json:"categories"` // top-level -> description
43		Paths       []PathDef         `json:"paths"`
44	}
45	
46	type PathDef struct {
47		Path        string   `json:"path"`
48		Description string   `json:"description"`
49		Examples    []string `json:"examples,omitempty"`
50	}
51	
52	// normalizeFactText, factRecordID, validFactPath, and normalizeFactPaths moved
53	// to factmerge (NormalizeText/RecordID/ValidPath/NormalizePaths); the
54	// CLI names are forwarding wrappers in facts_aliases.go.
55	
56	// TopLevel returns the top-level category of a taxonomy path (the segment
57	// before the first dot), or "" if the path is empty.
58	func TopLevel(path string) string {
59		if i := strings.IndexByte(path, '.'); i >= 0 {
60			return path[:i]
61		}
62		return path
63	}
64	
65	// --- on-disk layout -------------------------------------------------------
66	
67	// BranchRelDir returns the brain-relative directory holding a branch's
68	// facts. The readable slug alone is not collision-free — distinct branches can
69	// sanitize to the same slug (e.g. "evis/search" and "evis-search", or "Main"
70	// and "main") — and two branches sharing a facts file would clobber each other
71	// and break branch isolation. A short hash of the full branch name is appended
72	// so each branch maps to a stable, unique directory while staying greppable.
73	func BranchRelDir(branch string) string {
74		slug := base.SafePathComponent(branch, "branch", 80)
75		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(branch))
76		return filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(DirName, slug+"-"+hex.EncodeToString(sum[:4])))
77	}
78	
79	func FileRelPath(branch string) string {
80		return filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(BranchRelDir(branch), FileName))
81	}
82	
83	// BranchStoreExists reports whether the brain actually holds a facts.ndjson
84	// for a branch.
85	//
86	// Load deliberately returns an empty slice for a missing file so first-run
87	// callers need no special case, which means every read surface reports a
88	// misspelled branch exactly as it reports a real branch with nothing on it.
89	// Wherever that difference matters — naming a promote endpoint, say — this is
90	// the check that tells the two apart.
91	func BranchStoreExists(brainDir, branch string) bool {
92		if brainDir == "" || branch == "" {
93			return false
94		}
95		_, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(brainDir, filepath.FromSlash(FileRelPath(branch))))
96		if err == nil {
97			return true
98		}
99		s, present, readErr := readRepoFactStore(brainDir)
100		_, exists := s.Views[repoFactViewDir(branch)]
101		return present && readErr == nil && exists
102	}

1	package factstore
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"os"
6		"sort"
7		"strings"
8	
9		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/factmerge"
10		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/base"
11		bmanifest "github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/manifest"
12	)
13	
14	// integrity.go cross-checks the manifest's declared fact source against
15	// the facts the store can actually produce — both HOW MANY it produces and
16	// WHICH ones, because a corruption can leave the first right while destroying
17	// the second (see COUNTS ARE NOT ENOUGH below).
18	//
19	// sources.facts in the manifest is a CLAIM: "this brain holds N facts". Every
20	// health surface printed that claim as though it were an observation, and
21	// nothing ever compared it to the store. A facts.ndjson that had gone lossy —
22	// a line overwritten with valid JSON that is not a fact record, a truncated
23	// file, a botched hand edit — therefore kept reporting N on `status`, `doctor`
24	// and `facts map` while recall returned fewer, `get fact:<id>` said "not
25	// found", and `search` volunteered that the answer "may genuinely not be in
26	// the brain". For a durable-memory product that last line converts silent data
27	// loss into an affirmative false statement.
28	//
29	// The history index already solves this and its wording is the model:
30	//
31	//	history index size does not match the manifest; run `entire brain refresh
32	//	history` to rebuild it
33	//
34	// Note WHERE that check lives. It is not inside the per-record reader; it is
35	// in the function that loads the artifact the manifest declares, so every
36	// caller of that artifact inherits it and the REBUILD path — which must be
37	// able to run against the damaged artifact — does not. Facts need the same
38	// shape, and Load is the wrong seam for three reasons:
39	//
40	//  1. Load is per-branch and the manifest records only a total across
41	//     branches, so Load cannot know what N is for the branch it is
42	//     reading.
43	//  2. Its ~30 callers include distill, remember, facts gc/promote/merge and
44	//     refresh — the very commands that REPAIR a lossy store. A loader that
45	//     failed closed would wedge the store shut with no way out.
46	//  3. The manifest's count is produced by LoadAllBranches (see
47	//     updateFactSourceManifestLocked). Checking the claim with the same
48	//     function that produced it makes the check an exact inverse: no
49	//     branch-name-to-directory ambiguity, and any disagreement is real.
50	//
51	// So the check lives here, beside MissingBranchStores — the existing seam
52	// for "the manifest names something the store cannot produce" — and every
53	// surface reads one report. The retrieval note inherits through the single
54	// emptyResultBlindSpot choke point, which covers recall, search, query and
55	// retrieve at once.
56	
57	// COUNTS ARE NOT ENOUGH. The first cut of this check compared Declared against
58	// Readable and nothing else, which leaves a corruption that PRESERVES the count
59	// completely invisible: overwrite one line of facts.ndjson with a copy of
60	// another and the store still yields N records, still parses, still declares N
61	// — and the fact whose line was taken is gone. `get fact:<id>` says "not
62	// found", doctor says "facts: ok", and `search` goes back to volunteering that
63	// the answer "may genuinely not be in the brain". That is the same affirmative
64	// false statement this file exists to eliminate, reached by a different route.
65	//
66	// The obvious repair — compare the declared id SET against the readable one —
67	// is not available: sources.facts records counts (facts/distilled/authored/
68	// superseded/by_kind), never ids, and putting ids there would not help. That
69	// manifest is re-derived from the store itself by SummarizeSource on every
70	// mutating remember, refresh, gc, promote and retract, so a declared id set would
71	// re-baseline onto the damage at the next write exactly as the count does, and
72	// would cry loss on every legitimate id-changing operation in between.
73	//
74	// What IS checkable from the store alone, with no bookkeeping and nothing that
75	// can go stale, is the invariant the store is written under: WITHIN ONE BRANCH
76	// AN ID IDENTIFIES EXACTLY ONE FACT. Every writer keys by id before it writes
77	// (factmerge.Upsert, factmerge.Promote via IndexOf, factmerge.GC), so a branch
78	// that yields the same id twice was not written by this program. The second
79	// record did not join the fact set; it stands where a different fact used to
80	// be. That is loss, and it is loss the count cannot see.
81	//
82	// Per BRANCH, emphatically not per brain. A fact id is sha256 of normalized
83	// text plus sorted paths (factmerge.RecordID) — the branch is not in it — so
84	// the same fact carried between branches keeps its id, which is precisely what
85	// `facts promote` does on purpose. A brain-wide id set would report data loss
86	// on every promote, and a check that cries loss on a legitimate operation is
87	// worse than the hole it closes.
88	
89	// DefectMode names WHICH way the store fails the manifest. They are
90	// different user situations and must not collapse into one sentence: "not
91	// built" is a rebuild, "corrupt" is a repair, "lossy" is data that is gone and
92	// has to be re-distilled, and "duplicated" is data that was overwritten while
93	// the numbers stayed right.
94	type DefectMode string
95	
96	const (
97		// DefectNone is a store that can produce what the manifest declares.
98		DefectNone DefectMode = ""
99		// DefectMissing: a declared branch has no facts.ndjson at all.
100		// Already detected by MissingBranchStores; kept in its own words.
101		DefectMissing DefectMode = "missing"
102		// DefectUnreadable: a line will not parse. The store is corrupt
103		// and nothing on the branch can be read, not just the bad line.
104		DefectUnreadable DefectMode = "unreadable"
105		// DefectLossy: every line parses, but the store yields fewer
106		// facts than the manifest declares. This is the readable-but-short case —
107		// the one that used to pass every health surface.
108		DefectLossy DefectMode = "lossy"
109		// DefectStale: the store yields MORE facts than the manifest
110		// declares. Not data loss — the manifest is behind — but still a declared
111		// number that was never observed, so it is reported rather than printed.
112		DefectStale DefectMode = "stale"
113		// DefectDuplicated: every line parses and the counts are not
114		// short, but one branch stores the same fact id twice. Deliberately NOT
115		// folded into "lossy": lossy is a SHORTFALL — fewer facts than claimed,
116		// repaired by re-distilling what is missing — while this is a
117		// SUBSTITUTION, where the arithmetic is intact and a specific fact was
118		// overwritten by a copy of its neighbour. Telling the two apart is the
119		// difference between "some of your memory did not survive" and "this
120		// particular record is standing in for one that is gone".

283	// Inspect cross-checks a declared fact source against the store on
284	// disk. A nil source is a brain with no facts declared: nothing is claimed, so
285	// nothing can be lost, and the result is healthy. That is what keeps a
286	// genuinely empty brain from reporting loss.
287	func Inspect(brainDir string, source *bmanifest.FactSource) Integrity {
288		if brainDir == "" || source == nil {
289			return Integrity{}
290		}
291		report := Integrity{Declared: source.Facts, Pending: source.PendingReconcile}
292	
293		// Mode 1 — not built. A declared branch with no facts.ndjson is the
294		// already-handled case; keep its more specific message rather than folding
295		// it into the count mismatch it would also produce.
296		if missing := MissingBranchStores(brainDir, source); len(missing) > 0 {
297			report.Missing = missing
298			report.Mode = DefectMissing
299			return report
300		}
301	
302		// Mode 2 — corrupt. LoadAllBranches is the same function
303		// updateFactSourceManifestLocked used to PRODUCE source.Facts, so a
304		// disagreement below is a real one and not a re-derivation artifact.
305		// Validate declared paths through the same guarded reader used by recall
306		// before the aggregate loader opens any of those stores.
307		if broken := UnreadableBranchStores(brainDir, source); len(broken) > 0 {
308			report.ParseError = broken[0].Err.Error()
309			for _, store := range broken {
310				report.Unreadable = append(report.Unreadable, store.Branch)
311			}
312			report.Mode = DefectUnreadable
313			return report
314		}
315		byFile, err := LoadStoreFiles(brainDir)
316		if err != nil {
317			report.ParseError = err.Error()
318			for _, broken := range UnreadableBranchStores(brainDir, source) {
319				report.Unreadable = append(report.Unreadable, broken.Branch)
320			}
321			report.Mode = DefectUnreadable
322			return report
323		}
324		duplicated := map[string]struct{}{}
325		for _, records := range byFile {
326			// One `seen` per store FILE, never one for the whole brain: a file is
327			// the set `Load` hands to recall, so a repeat within one file is
328			// the only shape that shadows a memory. The same id across files is
329			// ordinary: `facts promote` copies a record into another branch's
330			// store, and the hosted pull mirrors the repo feed into the current
331			// branch's store. Bucketing by the branch recorded on each record
332			// conflated those mirrors into one bucket and reported them as
333			// corruption (COR-2220).
334			seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(records))
335			for _, record := range records {
336				if !IsFactRecord(record) {
337					report.Unusable++
338					continue
339				}
340				report.Readable++
341				if _, repeat := seen[record.ID]; repeat {
342					duplicated[record.ID] = struct{}{}
343					continue
344				}
345				seen[record.ID] = struct{}{}
346				report.Distinct++
347			}
348		}
349		if len(duplicated) > 0 {
350			report.DuplicateIDs = make([]string, 0, len(duplicated))
351			for id := range duplicated {
352				report.DuplicateIDs = append(report.DuplicateIDs, id)
353			}
354			sort.Strings(report.DuplicateIDs)
355		}
356	
357		// Mode 3 — readable but short (or long).
358		switch {
359		case report.Readable < report.expected(), report.Unusable > 0:
360			report.Mode = DefectLossy
361		// Mode 4 — readable, and the arithmetic is not short, but a branch holds
362		// one id twice. This runs BEFORE the stale test on purpose: a duplicate
363		// that was appended rather than written over also makes the store longer
364		// than the manifest, and "the manifest is behind the store — run refresh"
365		// is the one piece of advice that must not be given here. Refreshing
366		// re-derives the count from the collided store, declares it, and the
367		// brain goes quiet about a fact it can no longer produce.
368		case len(report.DuplicateIDs) > 0:
369			report.Mode = DefectDuplicated
370		case report.Readable > report.expected():
371			report.Mode = DefectStale
372		}
373		return report
374	}

379	// manifest's own health is a separate check that owns that message.

Factstore core of PR 2 implemented on `evisdren/flat-repo-fact-store`; package-scoped, not committed, all gates green.

**Final API surface**
- `Load(brainDir string) ([]factmerge.Record, error)` — flat store **plus** an in-memory, read-only fold of every legacy source (v1 store views with overrides; legacy branch NDJSON files, including post-migration stragglers). `factmerge.Sort` order; corrupt and forward-version stores fail closed.
- `Write(brainDir string, records []factmerge.Record) error` — refuses records without an id; refuses to replace a forward-version store; atomic replace of `facts/store.json` (schema 3, `{"schema_version":3,"records":{id: record}}`); then parks remaining legacy dirs (safe by the load-mutate-write-under-brain-lock contract; an id the caller removed on purpose must not resurrect from an unmaintained file).
- `MigrateRepository(brainDir string) (MigrationSummary, error)` — standing idempotent reconcile: fold → write → **verify** (re-read, every folded id present; failure leaves legacy dirs untouched) → park dirs to `facts/.legacy-<unixts>/<dir>/` (rename, never delete; damaged/unfoldable lines survive there). No-op (no write) when flat and clean.
- `MigrationSummary{Folded int, StragglerFiles int, MovedDirs []string}` + `Changed() bool`. `StragglerFiles > 0` = a released binary wrote after migration — callers should tell the user to update that machine.
- `SummarizeSource(now, records []factmerge.Record, chunksScanned, chunksDistilled, proposals int, warnings)` — flat; `Branches` stays empty (field kept for old manifests).
- Fold semantics: by content id, provenance union via `Upsert`; explicit lifecycle resolution (`Upsert` alone keeps the stored side's status, which is order-dependent): retirement > active > candidate, except a **strictly newer** active copy revives a retirement; order-independent, tested both fold orders.
- `Inspect` adapted to the flat view (missing/unreadable/lossy/stale); the old duplicate-id substitution corruption is now caught structurally — a map key over a different record's body fails `decodeV3` closed.

**Deleted**: views machinery (`replaceView`/`compact`/`view`/projection publishing), `NativeProjection`, `RollbackRepository`, `RepositoryViewDirs`, `BranchStoreExists`, `MissingBranchStores`, `UnreadableBranchStores(+type)`, `MissingStoreWarning(ForBranch)`, `LoadAllBranches`, `LoadStoreFiles`, `WriteStoreFile`, `OtherBranchBlindSpot`, `BranchRelDir`, `FileRelPath`, all of `files.go`. **Kept**: taxonomy, locus, global store (flipped to flat `Load`; same layout, same migration), `CleanupRepositoryTemps`, `RepositoryStatus` (Views now counts unmigrated legacy dirs; JSON keys unchanged), v1 decode helpers as unexported migration-only code in `repo_fact_compat.go` with a delete-when-releases-die header.

**Manifest**: `SchemaVersion` 4 → 5 with a comment recording the one-way-door rationale and the verified released-binary half-write behavior. `MinSchemaVersion` untouched; manifest package tests pass.

**Tests**: migration matrix (a)–(f) all implemented — schema-1 with view overrides, marker+legacy files (parks only after verify, originals survive under the park, second pass no-op), flat+straggler (summary observable), mixed, retirement-wins (3 timestamp cases × both fold orders) plus active-beats-candidate, and fail-closed on read-only FS and on corrupt legacy files with sources untouched. Flat round-trip, forward-version, substitution-corruption, no-id refusal, park-on-write, read-only-fold, randomized no-loss walk, fuzz round-trip. The three `TestRepoFactStoreReleased*` tests (what `scripts/test-memory-storage-compat.sh` runs) are rewritten to the flat contract at package level — released binary writes/retractions fold, migration parks, stragglers fold with `StragglerFiles` reported. `go test -race` green (2.8 s), `go vet` and `gofmt -l -s` clean.

1. `Write` refuses to overwrite a forward-version store — your spec gated only reads; without this, a newer build's store could be destroyed by an older flat-aware build.

The released-binary tests previously asserted CLI-level branch visibility and `memories storage migrate/rollback` round-trips via the CURRENT binary; that contract is gone and the current binary doesn't build until you flip callers. I rewrote them package-level (released binary for writes, package API for assertions) — **cli-level released-compat coverage must be re-established in `internal/cli`'s compat suite when you flip the callers**, including the "current binary's remember bumps the manifest and the old binary warns" behavior.
